questions.question_text: A shop receives $29$ boxes with $16$ mugs in each box. How many mugs arrive?

options.why: Added the number of boxes and mugs per box instead of multiplying.
Multiplied by only the ones digit 6 and ignored the tens in 16.
Rounded 29 boxes to 30 but did not adjust to the exact total.

questions.question_text: An orchard plants $42$ rows of $23$ trees. How many trees are planted?

options.why: Added rows and trees per row instead of finding equal groups.
Multiplied 42 by only the ones digit 3 in 23.
Rounded 42 down to 40 and used the estimate as the exact answer.

questions.question_text: A musician practises for $28$ minutes each day for $34$ days. How many minutes does she practise?

options.why: Added the daily minutes and number of days instead of multiplying.
Used only the ones digit 4 from the number of days.
Rounded 34 days to 30 and did not correct the estimate.

questions.question_text: A storage room has $72$ racks. Each rack holds $15$ helmets. How many helmets can be stored?

options.why: Added the racks and helmets per rack instead of multiplying.
Multiplied by only the ones digit 5 and omitted the ten in 15.
Rounded 72 racks to 70 and reported the estimate as exact.

questions.question_text: A chef fills $56$ packets with $32$ biscuits in each packet. Which calculation finds the total number of biscuits?

options.why: Added the two quantities instead of combining 56 equal groups.
Found a difference even though the situation asks for equal groups altogether.
Divided the number of packets by their size instead of finding the total.

questions.question_text: There are $14$ crates. Each crate holds $18$ cartons, and each carton holds $5$ jars. How many jars are there?

options.why: Found the number of cartons but did not multiply by 5 jars per carton.
Found jars in one crate but omitted the 14 crates.
Added the three quantities instead of multiplying the nested equal groups.

questions.question_text: A college has $26$ classes of $24$ students. Each student needs $3$ folders. There are also $5$ offices. How many folders are needed for students?

options.why: Treated the 5 offices as extra classes even though they contain no students in the question.
Found the number of students but omitted 3 folders for each student.
Multiplied classes by folders per student but omitted 24 students per class.
